prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Kit. Zoe MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Stop the Drum; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: Kit sits beside a single small drum secured on a low stand in a quiet bright music corner. The drum is open at the bottom, with one taut synthetic pale drumhead.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One plain red cylindrical drum, cream taut drumhead and navy rim, fixed securely on a low navy stand; Kit uses his right palm to tap or rest on the head; no stick, mallet, second drum or floating hand; Small curved motion marks represent quick movement; they are diagrams, never cracks or extra drum skins
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: First tap made; right hand lifting clear; one drum.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Kit’s right palm is just above the center of the cream head after one gentle tap. Left hand rests on his own knee. Drum and stand stable. One short motion tick at the head; no mallet.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.
Production finish: every surface must be perfectly flat, clean digital cel color with smooth crisp outlines. ZERO paper grain, speckling, stipple, dither, paint, canvas fibers, mottling, scuffs or noisy gradients anywhere, including skin, rug, walls, table, floor and shadows. Prefer solid flat fills; any small shadow is one smooth flat shape. This is polished vector-like raster art, never a textured watercolor print.

visualReview.note: Inspected board: Kit in locked cast clothes; one red cylindrical drum design with cream taut head, navy rim and stable low stand; no sticks. Relaxed right-hand tapping reference is usable. Reference includes a framed music-note decoration; final page prompts must exclude written notes and that decoration, and follow each exact hand/state brief.
